questions.stem: If the cost price of \(15\) articles is equal to the selling price of \(12\) articles, then what is the profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Given: CP of \(15\) articles = SP of \(12\) articles
Using formula: Profit% = \(\frac{a-b}{b} \times 100\) where CP of \(a\) articles = SP of \(b\) articles
Here \(a = 15, b = 12\)
Profit% = \(\frac{15-12}{12} \times 100 = \frac{3}{12} \times 100 = 25\)%

questions.stem: If the cost price of \(x\) articles equals the selling price of \(y\) articles, and there is a profit of \(25\)%, then find the ratio \(x:y\).
questions.keySolution:
Given: Profit = \(25\)%
Using the formula: If CP of \(x\) articles = SP of \(y\) articles
Profit% = \(\frac{x-y}{y} \times 100\)
\(25 = \frac{x-y}{y} \times 100\)
\(0.25 = \frac{x-y}{y}\)
\(0.25y = x - y\)
\(1.25y = x\)
\(x:y = 5:4\)

questions.stem: A dealer buys goods worth ₹\(10,000\). The cost price of \(50\) items equals the selling price of \(40\) items. If he sells all the goods, what will be his total profit?
questions.keySolution:

questions.stem: If the cost price of \(m\) articles equals the selling price of \(n\) articles, where \(m > n\), then the profit percentage is:
questions.keySolution:
When CP of \(m\) articles = SP of \(n\) articles
Let CP of each article = ₹\(1\)
CP of \(m\) articles = ₹\(m\)
SP of \(n\) articles = ₹\(m\)
SP of each article = ₹\(\frac{m}{n}\)
Profit per article = ₹\(\frac{m}{n} - ₹1 = ₹\frac{m-n}{n}\)
Profit% = \(\frac{\frac{m-n}{n}}{1} \times 100 = \frac{m-n}{n} \times 100\)
